# Batch 35 — Watermark investigation + click-to-edit existing text

Searched thoroughly for the reported watermark:

- `grep -rn "Generated by AWE-OS"` across the whole client: 2 hits, neither

- Traced the actual download path (`index.jsx`'s `handleDownload` →

No code change made. Owner confirmed (2026-07-30) they're not sure where

## 2. Real inline text editing — pdf-lib cannot do this; built the honest alternative

Checked pdf-lib's actual API: it can only *add* new content (`drawText`,
`drawRectangle`, etc.) and do structural operations (merge, copy pages, fill
AcroForms, encrypt). There is no API to find or replace text already drawn
on a page — no content-stream parser, no glyph-level editing. This is a
fundamental limitation, not a missing setting: PDF text is stored as
positioned glyph-drawing operators against often-*subsetted* fonts (only
the glyphs actually used are embedded), so a literal "replace this text"
operation can require characters that don't exist in that font at all, and
PDF has no native reflow if the replacement text is a different length.
Professional editors that support this (Acrobat, Foxit, Soda PDF) have
built large proprietary content-stream engines over years — not something
to attempt on top of pdf-lib in a single batch.

**What was built instead** (owner-approved): PDF.js's `getTextContent()`
does expose existing text with real position/size data (the same API any
PDF.js-based viewer uses for text selection/search). Clicking existing text
with the Text tool now:

1. Hit-tests the click against that page's text items (converted to
   RENDER_SCALE canvas-pixel boxes using the same transform math PDF.js's
   own `TextLayerBuilder` uses internally — `Util.transform(viewport.
   transform, item.transform)`).
2. On a hit: creates a Whiteout annotation covering that exact box, plus a
   Text annotation pre-filled with the original string, at the same
   position/size — as one batched, single-undo action (new
   `useAnnotations.addAnnotations`, plural).
3. Focuses the new text box immediately for editing.
4. Clicking empty space still falls through to the existing blank-box
   placement, unchanged.

This is explicitly **cover + pre-filled overlay, not content-stream
editing** — the original text remains in the PDF underneath (same
disclosed limitation as Whiteout already has). It looks and feels like
inline editing without claiming to do something the underlying library
can't.

## Known limitations (by design, not bugs)

- Only unrotated text is hit-testable (rotated/skewed runs are skipped
  rather than mis-measured) — most real-world PDFs are unrotated, but a
  rotated caption/stamp text won't be click-to-edit-able this way.
- Granularity is per PDF.js text *run* (often a full line), not per-word.
- Clicking the exact same original spot twice creates a second overlapping
  whiteout+text pair (harmless visually — same result — but wastes an
  annotation). Re-editing an already-patched spot should go through Select
  + click the new text annotation instead of the Text tool again.

## Bug found during QA (fixed)

Same root cause as v1's historical focus bug (see project memory): the new
text box wasn't actually focusable. The existing blank-box-placement path
defers creating+focusing the annotation to `pointerup` (after the click's
own default mousedown focus-shift has already settled) — this new path
creates and focuses synchronously on `pointerdown`, which is exactly when
the browser's default focus handling is active, and it silently stole
focus back afterward. Fixed with `e.preventDefault()` on that specific
branch, matching the historical fix.

## Verification

Playwright click-through: click existing text → whiteout+text created (one
batched undo step) → new box focused and pre-filled with the original
string → typing replaces it → empty-space click still places a normal
blank box (regression check) → download still produces a valid PDF. All
pass; zero new console errors (one pre-existing, unrelated CORS warning
from `useTrackToolView` hitting the prod API from localhost, present on
every tool page).
